newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end up, small stocks in limelight.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end up, small stocks in limelight.

text.p: Singapore shares ended firmer on Friday in a technical rebound after recent sharp falls and with retail buyers homing in on penny stocks, dealers said.
Institutional bargain-hunting for index-linked shares also helped the index regain upward momentum.
The 30-share Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) recaptured some lustre to end 23.54 points higher at 1,985.94.
The revival of Cerebos Pacific by 15 cents to Singapore $6.00, and Keppel Corp by 25 cents to S$6.45, was seen a major bolster to the index.
The unweighted STII had been languishing around two-and-a-half year lows for a week.
"The buying was much more broad-based this time. There was a bit of accumulation going on," a local bank dealer said.
But the bulk of volume was confined to second-liners and Malaysian over-the-counter issues with retail buyers showing a bigger presence than institutions, dealers said.
Leading the actives was Berjaya industrial, up 33 cents to S$1.66. Some attributed the buying spree to rumours over its upcoming full year results.
Tye Soon hit a high of S$0.585 and later ended at S$0.565, up half a cent, on turnover of nine million shares.
New-listed New Toyo, Excel Machine and food company FHTK also reached record highs in busy action.
